## Statement of Need

The online sexual exploitation of children has reached a scale that outpaces
every prior era of child protection. In 2024, the National Center for Missing &
Exploited Children's CyberTipline received more than 546,000 reports of online
enticement — roughly a 192% increase over 2023 and a twelve-fold increase since
2021. [T-02] The trend has not slowed: in just the first half of 2025, online
enticement reports rose another 77% year over year, from 292,951 to 518,720.
[T-04] Financial sextortion — a form of enticement that overwhelmingly targets
teenage boys — reached nearly 100 reports per day in 2024 and climbed to an
average of 137 per day in 2025. Its human cost is measured in lives: at least
three dozen U.S. teenagers have died by suicide since 2021 after being
victimized. [T-03]

The threat is also mutating faster than the systems built to counter it.
Generative-AI-related child exploitation reports to NCMEC surged 1,325% in 2024,
climbing to more than 67,000, and then to 440,419 in the first half of 2025 — a
category of harm that did not meaningfully exist three years ago. [T-05] At the
same time, the 2024 REPORT Act, by requiring online platforms to report child
sex trafficking for the first time, has begun to expose its true online scale:
CyberTipline child-sex-trafficking reports rose from 5,976 in the first half of
2024 to 62,891 in the first half of 2025. [T-04]

These national trends are not abstractions in the region Project Harmony serves.
Landmark prevalence research on Nebraska's commercial sex market — the
data-science analysis by Creighton University's Human Trafficking Initiative —
found that roughly 900 individuals are advertised for sex online in the state
each month, often multiple times, with about 75% showing indicators of potential
trafficking and 15% at high risk. [T-01] The formal identification data tell the
same story on a bi-state footprint: in 2024 the National Human Trafficking
Hotline identified 71 trafficking cases in Nebraska and 88 in Iowa — the two
states from which Project Harmony draws the children it serves as the accredited
Children's Advocacy Center for the Omaha metro, eastern Nebraska, and
southwest Iowa. [T-06]

The response that works is coordinated, and it begins upstream with prevention
education. A quasi-experimental evaluation of a youth trafficking-prevention
curriculum found measurable gains in commercial-sexual-exploitation awareness
and in young people's help-seeking self-efficacy. [E-1] A systematic review of
education and awareness interventions to prevent online child sexual abuse
similarly found consistent improvements in online-safety knowledge — while
candidly noting the limits of knowledge-only approaches, which is precisely why
MATYS pairs prevention education with the identification, advocacy, and
multidisciplinary response capacity of an accredited Children's Advocacy Center.
[E-2] Federal investment in MATYS extends a proven model to meet a threat that
is accelerating faster than any single community can absorb alone.

## Honest Draft integrity report

**All six evidence claims are VERIFIED-WEB (verify run 2026-07-03).** Framing
guards to apply before submission:

- **T-01 (Nebraska market):** 2017 Backpage-era data — present as "landmark
  prevalence research," not a current count, and pair with the current national
  trend (T-02/T-04). NOTE: the engine corrected an error carried in the original
  corpus — the ~75% figure means "show indicators of trafficking," not "are
  Nebraskans." Restored figure: ~900/month (primary report).
- **T-03 (sextortion):** "at least 36" is a floor and counts teenagers
  (predominantly boys); cite the year for the per-day rate (~100/day in 2024,
  137/day in 2025).
- **T-04 / T-06 (reporting-mandate & hotline):** these reflect reporting/contact
  volume — amplified by the REPORT Act (T-04) and limited to those who contacted
  the Hotline (T-06). Frame as "reports" / "identified cases," never as
  prevalence.
- **T-02 / T-05:** CyberTipline totals are reporting volume (amplified by the
  REPORT Act and by AI firms newly implementing detection), not solely rising
  prevalence.

**Human accountability:** a qualified Project Harmony reviewer must verify every
figure and own every submitted word before this draft leaves the building.
